cheatsheet:
**Arrays**
`int cargo[4] = {12, 7, 30, 5};` · indexes run 0 to 3 · `cargo[0]` first · unlisted values start at 0

**Never go past the end**
C doesn't check. Reading `cargo[4]` gives garbage or a crash.

**Strings**
A `char` array ending with `'\0'`. `char ship[] = "KERNEL";` holds 7 chars. Print with `%s`. Read one word with `scanf("%s", name);` (no `&`).

**string.h**
`strlen(s)` length · `strcpy(dest, src)` copy · `strcmp(a, b) == 0` equal. Never compare strings with `==`.

**sizeof**
`sizeof(x)` is the size in bytes. `(int)sizeof(arr) / (int)sizeof(arr[0])` is an array's length.

**2D**
`int grid[2][3];` · `grid[row][col]`

lessons.title: Rows of boxes
lessons.concept:
An **array** is a row of boxes of the same type under one name: `int cargo[4] = {12, 7, 30, 5};`

Boxes are numbered from **0**: `cargo[0]` is the first, `cargo[3]` the last. There is no `cargo[4]`.

A `for` loop is the natural partner: `for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)` visits every box.

C never checks the index for you. Reading past the end gives garbage, or crashes.

predict.prompt: Before you run it: type what it prints.
predict.explain: Index 0 is the first box, index 3 the last of four. The loop adds all four.

drills.explain: Counting from 0: a[0] is 4, a[1] is 8.
Boxes you don't list in `{ }` start at 0.

drills.prompt: It reads 5 readings and should print the biggest. It works for normal readings but says `0` when they're all negative. Fix it.
drills.explain: Starting at 0 assumes something is bigger than 0. Start with the first reading instead: `best = r[0]`.

drills.prompt: Read 5 numbers into an array, then print them in reverse order on one line, separated by spaces.
drills.explain: One loop to fill, one loop counting down from index 4 to 0 to print. A space at the end of the line is fine.

lessons.title: Text is an array of characters
lessons.concept:
C has no special text type. A **string** is a `char` array with a hidden **`'\0'`** at the end that marks where the text stops.

`char ship[] = "KERNEL";` holds 7 chars: 6 letters plus `'\0'`. `sizeof(ship)` (the size in bytes) is 7.

Print a string with `%s`. Read one word with `scanf("%s", name);`. No `&` here: an array's name already tells scanf where it is.

predict.prompt: Before you run it: type what it prints.
predict.explain: The loop counts characters until it reaches the `'\0'` marker, which isn't counted.

drills.prompt: How many chars does `s` take up?
drills.explain: 3 letters plus the `'\0'` at the end.
A string is just an array, so you can change one letter by its index.

drills.prompt: Read one word into `name`. (Arrays don't need `&`.)
drills.explain: The array's name already tells scanf where it starts.

drills.prompt: Read one word (at most 50 letters) and print how many times the lowercase letter `a` appears in it.
drills.explain: Walk the string until `'\0'` and count each `'a'` (single quotes: one char).

lessons.title: Text tools and grids
lessons.concept:
`#include <string.h>` gives you text tools:
`strlen(s)` the length · `strcpy(dest, src)` copies src into dest · `strcmp(a, b)` is `0` when they match.

Never compare strings with `==`. That compares **where** they live, not what they say.

Arrays can have two dimensions, like a grid: `int grid[2][3];` is 2 rows of 3. `grid[1][2]` is row 1, column 2.

predict.prompt: Before you run it: type the three lines it prints.
predict.explain: "dock" has 4 letters; after the copy they match (true is 1); row 1 column 2 is 6.

drills.prompt: Which line copies the text in `src` into `dest`?
drills.explain: Destination first, like `dest = src` would read. Plain `=` doesn't work on arrays.

drills.prompt: It should say `ACCESS` when the password is `OPEN` and `LOCKED` otherwise. It always says `LOCKED`. Fix it.
drills.explain: `==` asks whether they're the same array in memory, which they never are. `strcmp(word, "OPEN") == 0` compares the letters. It needs `#include <string.h>`.

checkpoint.prompt: Which indexes can you use with `int a[4];`?
Fill in the placeholder letter that prints a string.
What marks the end of every C string?
checkpoint.explain: The zero character. It's why "HI" takes 3 chars.
